01.r: Pronounces a curse on the man described.
01.n: A passive participle, the form used in curses, as the brief's lexicon notes: 'cursed be he'. Gesenius: TO CURSE.

02.r: The man who cheats God of what he promised.
02.n: A participle, 'one acting deceitfully'. Gesenius: TO ACT FRAUDULENTLY, citing this very verse, Mal. 1:14. The Hebrew has no article; English needs one here.

03.r: States the deceiver's situation: he has a sound male to give.
03.n: Literally 'and there is': a word of existence, 'there is', used for 'to be'. Most translations make the clause 'who has'.

05.r: A male animal, fit to be offered.
05.n: Gesenius: a male, of men and of animals. The BSB adds 'acceptable', reading the male as the proper animal for his vow.

06.r: He promises an animal to God.
06.n: A participle, like the verbs around it. Gesenius: to vow, to promise voluntarily to do or to give anything.

07.r: But what he actually sacrifices is not the male.
07.n: Gesenius: to slaughter animals, specially to slay in sacrifice.

08.r: An animal damaged or spoiled, not the sound male he had.
08.n: A passive participle of a verb meaning to destroy, to ruin, to corrupt; Gesenius lists ruin by wounding among its senses. The translations range from 'a corrupt thing' to 'a blemished thing' and 'a defective animal'.

09.r: God, to whom the sacrifice is made.
09.n: Here the Hebrew has the title אֲדֹנָי, 'the Lord', not the name rendered 'the LORD'. JPS writes 'the L-rd'.

10.r: Gives the reason the cheat is cursed.

12.r: A king greater than any governor.
12.n: Gesenius: great, of size, of number, and of importance.

13.n: The pronoun is written out and there is no verb: 'a great King, I'. The Hebrew puts the pronoun last, as YLT keeps it.

14.r: Marks the words as the LORD's.

15.r: The personal name of Israel's God.

16.r: The LORD as commander of armies.

17.r: God's name, standing for God himself as he is known.
17.n: The brief's lexicon lists name, reputation, fame and glory among the senses.

18.n: A participle of 'to fear' in a passive form: feared, to be feared, awesome. Gesenius traces the root to the sense TO TREMBLE.

19.r: Even the other peoples hold God's name in awe.
19.n: Gesenius: a people; the brief's lexicon notes the plural is usually of peoples other than Israel. The KJV and Geneva say 'the heathen', the DRC and ASV 'the Gentiles'.

02.n: ὃς ἦν δυνατός, 'who was able' or 'powerful', where the Hebrew has 'deceiver'. A likely explanation is that the translators read a similar Hebrew word meaning 'able'; that is an inference. The first word is printed ὸς in our Greek text, evidently ὃς.

03.n: Dictionary form supplied; the brief gives none. ὑπῆρχεν, 'there was'.

06.n: καὶ εὐχὴ αὐτοῦ ἐπʼ αὐτῷ, 'and his vow is upon it': the Greek makes the verb a noun.

08.n: Dictionary form supplied; the brief gives none. διεφθαρμένον, 'corrupted, ruined', the perfect passive participle of διαφθείρω.

16.n: Printed Ιαντοκράτωρ in our Greek text; evidently Παντοκράτωρ, 'Almighty', for 'of hosts'.

18.n: ἐπιφανής, 'manifest, glorious', where the Hebrew has 'feared'. The Hebrew words for 'feared' and 'seen' look alike, which may explain the choice; that is an inference. English 'epiphany' comes from the related noun.
